query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a major Pt substitution (≈50 at.%) into the FeCoNi alloy, followed by rapid thermal annealing, will trigger the formation of an L10 ordered phase that greatly enhances magnetic anisotropy and therefore dramatically increases the coercivity.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or a closely related HEA derivative) with high saturation magnetization and coercivity no greater than 100 Oe.
generation.intervention: Substitute approximately 50 at.% of the alloy with Pt and apply rapid thermal annealing post-deposition.
generation.conditions: Thin films prepared on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature, followed by rapid thermal annealing under controlled conditions (as documented in the supplied evidence).
generation.structural_mediator: Transformation from fcc structure to an L10 chemically ordered phase.
generation.mechanism: Pt incorporation promotes chemical ordering during the rapid thermal annealing, driving the alloy from a magnetically soft fcc phase to a hard magnetic L10 phase. This ordering increases the magnetic anisotropy, which in turn leads to a drastic increase in coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: A three orders of magnitude increase in coercivity relative to the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi, accompanied by enhanced magnetic anisotropy.
generation.baseline: The initial coercivity of <100 Oe observed in single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or analogous HEA derivatives) without Pt addition.
generation.boundary: Effect predicted in thin film samples processed via sputtering and rapid thermal annealing on oxidized Si substrates; outcome may depend on the precise composition and processing conditions unique to the HEA system under study.
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanism is supported by results in a similar system (FeCoNiMnCu with Pt), the direct applicability to simple FeCoNi alloys may vary due to differing elemental interactions and phase stability; further compositional and processing optimization may be required.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of thin film samples: one set of the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy and a second set with 50 at.% Pt substituted into the alloy. Both sets should be deposited on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates under identical conditions, then subjected to the same rapid thermal annealing protocol.
measurements: X-ray diffraction (XRD) to detect formation of the L10 ordered phase
Magnetic measurements (using a vibrating sample magnetometer, VSM) to quantify coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the Pt-substituted samples do not exhibit clear evidence of L10 ordering and do not show a coercivity increase of at least three orders of magnitude relative to the baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi films.

## Abstract
AbstractThe vast high entropy alloy (HEA) composition space is promising for discovery of new material phases with unique properties. This study explores the potential to achieve rare‐earth‐free high magnetic anisotropy materials in single‐phase HEA thin films. Thin films of FeCoNiMnCu sputtered on thermally oxidized Si/SiO2 substrates at room temperature are magnetically soft, with a coercivity on the order of 10 Oe. After post‐deposition rapid thermal annealing (RTA), the films exhibit a single face‐centered‐cubic phase, with an almost 40‐fold increase in coercivity. Inclusion of 50 at.% Pt in the film leads to ordering of a single L10 high entropy intermetallic phase after RTA, along with high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase. These results demonstrate a promising HEA approach to achieve high magnetic anisotropy materials using RTA.Keywords: high entropy alloy, magnetic anisotropy, rapid thermal annealing High entropy alloy (HEA) thin films are explored to achieve high magnetic anisotropy phases.
